rfi.title: Nepal’s deadly glacier collapse exposes climate risks across the Himalayas
rfi.description: A massive glacier collapse that triggered deadly flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border has exposed the growing dangers facing the rapidly warming Himalayas, where scientists say retreating ice and thawing ground are making mountain landscapes increasingly unstable.

rfi.title: Haiti families plead for release of hostages after deadly gang attack
rfi.description: Families in Kenscoff near the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince are demanding the release of relatives taken hostage by armed gangs during last weekend's deadly attack on the town. At least 47 people were killed and more than 20 abducted, with thousands having fled their homes to avoid further attacks.

rfi.title: EU joins aid effort as more than 1,300 remain missing after Nepal floods
rfi.description: The EU has joined international efforts to send aid after catastrophic floods on the Nepal-Tibet border left at least 360 people dead and more than 1,300 missing.

rfi.title: Former model sues French state over delay in Epstein recruiter rape investigation
rfi.description: A former model who accused an alleged recruiter for American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein of raping her in the 1990s is suing the French state for delays to the investigation. The state is also being sued by a child protection organisation, on behalf of alleged Epstein victims.

rfi.title: France to tie African development aid to efforts to limit migration to Mayotte
rfi.description: France plans to make its development aid to seven African countries conditional on greater cooperation in the fight against illegal immigration to the French island territory of Mayotte, as the issue becomes increasingly politicised ahead of the French presidential election next year.

rfi.title: Climate change is ‘very visible from space’, France's Sophie Adenot tells RFI
rfi.description: In an exclusive interview with RFI and sister TV channel France 24 from the International Space Station, French astronaut Sophie Adenot described the signs of climate change she can see from orbit and how she overcame major technical problems during her second spacewalk earlier this week.

rfi.title: Looking up: French sailors ditch GPS to rediscover celestial art of navigation
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the fourth of a five-part series, RFI meets amateur sailors learning to navigate by the stars, using a technique that allows them to find their position without GPS or onboard electronics.

rfi.title: Second person dies after man deliberately drives into crowd in Caen
rfi.description: A second person has died after a man deliberately drove his car into a group of people in the northern French city of Caen on Wednesday, leaving nine others injured.

rfi.title: Nigerian armed groups net nearly $6m in ransoms: study
rfi.description: Criminal groups in Nigeria raised nearly $6 million in ransom payments in the last year, a report said Wednesday, with two mass kidnappings by Boko Haram responsible for nearly 90 percent of the total.

rfi.title: France relaxes rules for three famous cheeses after summer drought
rfi.description: The drought in France is forcing farmers who produce milk for some of the country's most famous cheeses to feed their cows differently, as scorched pastures make it increasingly difficult to stick to strict rules on protected regional foods, known as AOP. Temporary exemptions on fodder sources will apply to the producers of Abondance, Beaufort and Comté to cope with the grass shortage.

rfi.title: Looking up: French collector gathers lunar photos that changed our view of space
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the last of a five-part series, space historian and collector Victor Martin-Malburet talks to RFI about his passion for Nasa's Moon missions and the photos they produced. He began searching around the world for original prints aged 15 and has now amassed a collection of 1,500 photographs.

rfi.title: French soldiers disciplined over Rhodesian flags linked to white supremacists
rfi.description: France's Ministry of the Armed Forces has launched disciplinary proceedings against several soldiers photographed holding flags linked to Rhodesia, a former white minority-ruled territory in southern Africa whose symbols have been embraced by white supremacists.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate left-wing mayor over alleged misuse of public funds
rfi.description: French financial prosecutors have opened an investigation into Bally Bagoyoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis, over suspected misuse of public funds during his employment by the Paris public transport operator RATP when he was also serving as a local elected official with the France Unbowed party.

rfi.title: French PM visits Mayotte to speed up 'slow' reconstruction after cyclone
rfi.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu arrives in the French overseas territory of Mayotte on Wednesday to try to speed up the reconstruction of the archipelago, 18 months after Cyclone Chido caused widespread destruction.

rfi.title: How Dolly Parton became much more than country music’s 'backwoods Barbie'
rfi.description: Back in 2008 at age 62, Dolly Parton released a single proclaiming she was "just a backwoods Barbie, too much makeup, too much hair."

rfi.title: Nigerian president orders rescue operation after mass kidnapping in mosque
rfi.description: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has ordered the military and other security agencies to launch an immediate rescue operation after the mass kidnapping of worshippers during an attack on a mosque in the north-central Niger State last week.

rfi.title: Looking up: Amateur meteorite hunters search for clues to origins of universe
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the third of a five-part series, RFI hears from volunteers in south-west France who are searching for meteorites as part of a citizen science project designed to help researchers recover fragments from space.

rfi.title: 'Shocking' book about Putin's private life wins French literary prize
rfi.description: A taboo-breaking book about Vladimir Putin's rise to power and private life, written by two exiled Russian journalists, won a newly established French literary prize on Tuesday.

euronews.title: EU tax: small Chinese parcels plunge 30 to 40%
euronews.description: Since 1 July, the EU has imposed a 3-euro customs duty on parcels under 150 euros. The move is already having an impact: imports, especially from China, have plunged by 30 to 40%.

france24fr.description: Double champion d'Europe, le PSG connaît désormais ses adversaires lors de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions, avec notamment le FC Barcelone et Manchester City au menu. Lens affrontera également les Citizens ainsi que Liverpool, tandis que Lille accueillera le Bayern Munich à Pierre-Mauroy et se rendra chez les champions anglais d'Arsenal.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : huit migrants tunisiens morts dans un naufrage en Méditerranée
france24fr.description: 🇹🇳 Douze migrants ont été retrouvés morts en Méditerranée après le naufrage d’une embarcation au large de la Tunisie. Parmi eux, huit ont été enterrées mercredi à Ben Gardane, près de la frontière libyenne.

france24fr.title: "La situation était devenue intenable" : pourquoi les FDS ont accepté leur dissolution en Syrie
france24fr.description: La dissolution des Forces démocratiques syriennes (FDS), prononcée mardi, marque un tournant majeur pour les Kurdes de Syrie, après plus d’une décennie d’autonomie militaire et politique. Retour sur les enjeux de l’accord conclu avec Damas et les raisons qui ont conduit Mazloum Abdi, le chef des forces kurdes, à accepter leur dissolution.

france24fr.title: Pakistan : les manifestations continuent dans l'Azad Cachemire malgré la répression et Internet coupé
france24fr.description: Des manifestations sévèrement réprimées secouent le Cachemire administré par le Pakistan depuis début juin. Elles ont notamment perturbé les élections législatives locales de juillet et d’août. Alors que l’accès à Internet a été coupé et que l'entrée des médias étrangers est restreinte, les habitants tentent de rendre compte de la situation sur le terrain.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : ce que les start-up attendent des candidats
france24fr.description: Le Medef veut du « courage » politique. À la Rencontre des entrepreneurs de France, son président Patrick Martin appelle les candidats à défendre davantage de liberté pour les entreprises, alors que le pessimisme domine chez les patrons. Mais qu’en est-il du côté des start-up et de la French Tech ? On en parle avec Julie Huguet, directrice de la Mission French Tech.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : à Ben Guerdane, les funérailles de huit migrants morts en mer
france24fr.description: À Ben Guerdane, ville tunisienne frontalière de la Libye, des habitants assistent aux funérailles de huit migrants morts en tentant de rejoindre l’Europe. Le bateau, qui transportait 15 migrants tunisiens, a coulé dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi au large de Zarzis, dans le sud-est de la Tunisie. Une personne a pu être secourue.

france24fr.title: "Le boucher de Bosnie" Ratko Mladic est mort, selon la télévision d'Etat serbe
france24fr.description: L'ex-chef militaire des Serbes de Bosnie Ratko Mladic, surnommé "Le boucher de Bosnie" pour son rôle dans le massacre de Srebrenica en 1995, est mort jeudi, a annoncé la chaîne de télévision publique serbe RTS.

france24fr.title: Au Sénégal, le pari d'un traitement contre la drépanocytose fabriqué en Afrique
france24fr.description: L'Afrique concentre près de 80 % de l'ensemble des cas de drépanocytose dans le monde. Aujourd'hui, le premier médicament générique fabriqué en Afrique pour traiter cette maladie fait naître l'espoir d'un meilleur traitement et d'une dépendance moindre vis-à-vis des médicaments onéreux importés d'Europe et d'Amérique.

france24fr.title: Crue meurtrière au Népal : le point sur la situation au lendemain du drame
france24fr.description: Plus de 1300 personnes, dont plusieurs centaines de touristes, sont portées disparues jeudi après les coulées de boue qui ont dévasté des vallées du Népal et de la région chinoise du Tibet, causant plus de 362 morts.

france24fr.title: Football : qui est Ayyoub Bouaddi, la nouvelle recrue de Manchester City ?
france24fr.description: ⚽️➡️Le club de Manchester City a recruté le Marocain Ayoub Bouaddi en provenance du Losc Lille. Le jeune milieu de terrain s’apprête à vivre une nouvelle aventure en Ligue 1 après s’être illustré avec les Lions de l’Atlas lors de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Exclusif : Sophie Adenot raconte le changement climatique vu depuis l'espace
france24fr.description: Dans une interview exclusive pour France 24, Sophie Adenot décrit depuis l’ISS les effets du changement climatique visibles depuis l'espace : une France plus sèche et jaunie en été, les fumées des incendies, des lacs qui s'assèchent et même des îles submergées.

france24fr.title: Fifa : l'UEFA prépare une plainte pour "gestion déloyale" contre Infantino
france24fr.description: L'UEFA prépare des poursuites judiciaires contre le président de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino, a-t-on appris jeudi de source proche du dossier. Selon cette source, l'instance continentale préparerait une plainte en droit suisse pour "gestion déloyale" en raison du controversé projet d'ouverture de la Coupe du monde à des investisseurs privés.

france24fr.title: Kenya : la découverte d’or dans un village attire les foules
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, la récente découverte d’or dans un petit village de montagne a provoqué une véritable ruée, attirant des milliers de personnes séduites par l’appât du gain.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : des cartes d’identité pour intégrer les réfugiés
france24fr.description: Il y a plus d’un million de réfugiés en Éthiopie. Jusqu’à présent, la majeure partie d’entre eux était cantonnée dans des camps. Grâce à un nouveau système de cartes d’identité, cette époque devrait bientôt être révolue. Liberté de mouvement, accès à l’éducation et au travail… le gouvernement éthiopien et le HCR tentent d’intégrer ces réfugiés à la société.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : une vidéo ravive les tensions xénophobes
france24fr.description: En Afrique du Sud, les tensions liées à la xénophobie n’ont pas disparu. Si le centre de rapatriement de Messina, dans le nord du pays, a été fermé, les mouvements anti-immigration, comme March and March, continuent d’appeler à manifester tous les jeudis pour réclamer l’expulsion de tous les sans-papiers. Sur les réseaux sociaux, une vidéo est également devenue virale.

france24fr.title: Gaza : comment Israël tente d’imposer son récit de la guerre
france24fr.description: Un an après la frappe israélienne contre l’hôpital Nasser, à Khan Younès, qui avait fait 22 morts, dont cinq journalistes, une enquête du Monde revient sur la communication mise en place par les autorités israéliennes après l’attaque. L’objectif : comprendre comment l’État hébreu tente d’imposer son récit et de présenter certaines victimes comme liées au Hamas. Alors, comment s’organise cette guerre de l’information ? Éclairage avec Amélie Férey, directrice des projets data à l’Institut de reche

Autobauer: Krisengespräche bei VW: Positive Signale in Chemnitz

Großer Polizeieinsatz: Opfer der Gewalttat sollen Ex-Freundin und Hausmeister sein
Fußball: Auslosung: Bayern-Trip an den Sehnsuchtsort - Kracher für RB
Auslosung der Vorrunde: Champions League: Bayern und BVB in Vorrunde gegen Arsenal
Das Ende der Sterne: Sollte man besser allein überleben? Oder gemeinsam?
zeit.description: Verstörend: Ridley Scotts neuer Film blickt von oben auf den postapokalyptischen Daseinskampf der Menschen.

zeit.title: Klage gegen OpenAI: Das Neinhorn und die Urheberrechtsklage
zeit.description: Der Carlsen-Verlag und Autor Marc-Uwe Kling verklagen OpenAI. KI scannt künftig an Berlins Kottbusser Tor. Waymo will Robotaxis nach München bringen. Der KI-Newsletter.

zeit.title: Auslosung Champions League: RB Leipzig in Königsklasse gegen Real Madrid und ManCity
Notarzteinsatz: Beeinträchtigungen beim S-Bahnverkehr in Frankfurt
Verbotene »Artgemeinschaft«: Razzia bei AfD-Landtagskandidaten wegen völkischer »Artgemeinschaft«
zeit.description: Ermittler gehen dem Verdacht nach, die 2023 verbotene »Artgemeinschaft« werde fortgeführt. Ermittelt wird gegen 15 Personen, darunter zwei AfD-Landtagskandidaten.

zeit.title: Brandenburg: Zwei Tote bei Gewalttat an Schule in Gosen-Neu Zittau
zeit.description: Bei einer Gewalttat an einer Schule in Brandenburg sind zwei Menschen getötet worden. Die Polizei nahm einen 19-Jährigen vorläufig fest.

zeit.title: Gerhard Feige: Der Bischof, mit dem die AfD zu kämpfen hat
zeit.description: Der Magdeburger Bischof Gerhard Feige will verhindern, dass die AfD die Regierung übernimmt. Die greift ihn persönlich an. Aber der Kirchenmann ist eben kein Anfänger.

zeit.title: Massaker von Srebrenica: Bosnisch-serbischer Kriegsverbrecher Ratko Mladić ist tot
zeit.description: Ratko Mladić gilt als Hauptverantwortlicher für den Völkermord von Srebrenica. Mit 84 Jahren stirbt der bosnisch-serbische Ex-General im UN-Gefängnis in Den Haag.

zeit.title: Sturzflut in Nepal: Sturzflut in Nepal – die schwierige Suche nach Überlebenden
zeit.description: Nach der Sturzflut in Nepal und Tibet gelten noch mehr als tausend Menschen als vermisst. Gibt es noch Hoffnung auf Überlebende? Und: Kriegsverbrecher Mladić ist tot.

nzz.title: Valérie Dittli verlässt die Waadtländer Mitte – und will eine eigene Partei gründen
nzz.description: In einem Interview mit der Zeitung «Le Temps» kündigt die umstrittene Staatsrätin die Gründung einer neuen Partei an.

nzz.title: Sina Frei im Short Track WM-Dritte – Gold an Österreicherin Stigger
nzz.description: Sina Frei gewinnt an der Mountainbike-WM in Val di Sole im Short Track die Bronzemedaille. Gold sichert sich die Österreicherin Laura Stigger. Die Schweizer Männer bleiben ohne Medaille.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Die Sturzflut von Nepal: Zahl der Toten steigt auf 389 +++ Zwei Schweizer laut EDA gerettet +++ Chinas Zentralbank sagt Millionen-Hilfe zu
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten reissen Wasser, Geröll und Eis alles in der Grenzregion zwischen China und Nepal mit sich. Mehr als 300 Menschen sterben, mehr als 1300 werden vermisst. Die wichtigsten Antworten zur Katastrophe im Himalaja-Tal.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Für die CDU ist alles zu spät
nzz.description: Lange hatte die Volkspartei die Möglichkeit, die AfD zu integrieren – doch sie liess Chance um Chance verstreichen. Nun hat sie nur noch schlechte Optionen.

nzz.title: Marc Lüthi ist neuer Präsident von Swiss Ice Hockey – kann der temperamentvolle Macher das Schweizer Eishockey befrieden?
nzz.description: Die Wahl des langjährigen CEO und Mitbesitzers des SC Bern wird personelle Folgen haben. Zunächst aber dürfte für einen Monat Waffenstillstand herrschen: International steht die nächste Wahl an.

nzz.title: Der Akademiker-Absturz: Sie sind häufiger erwerbslos als der Durchschnittsschweizer, oft nur befristet angestellt – und das auch noch in Teilzeit
nzz.description: Neue Zahlen des Bundesamts für Statistik zeichnen gerade für Universitätsabgänger ein düsteres Bild. Lohnt sich ein Studium noch?

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Gescheiterte Investorenpläne der Fifa: Die Uefa soll eine Strafanzeige gegen Infantino vorbereiten +++ Italien entzieht Infantino die Unterstützung
nzz.description: Die Fifa wollte einen Teil der kommerziellen Rechte an den Turnieren an private Investoren abgeben. Anfang August hat der Verband das Vorhaben zurückgezogen. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Der Chip-Gigant Nvidia wächst kräftig weiter – doch Anleger und Aufseher sorgen sich über heikle Kreislauf-Finanzierungen
nzz.description: Auch die jüngsten Quartalszahlen von Nvidia sind überaus positiv, die Gewinne sprudeln – dank KI und dem Bau von Rechenzentren. Derzeit machen Gerüchte die Runde, wonach Nvidia für 13 Milliarden Dollar Hugging Face übernehmen will, einen Marktplatz für Open-Source-KI.

nzz.title: Er befahl den Völkermord in Bosnien-Herzegowina: Jetzt ist der Kriegsverbrecher Ratko Mladic tot
nzz.description: Er sei zum Schutz Jugoslawiens und aller seiner Völker Offizier geworden, sagte Mladic vor dem Krieg. Danach wurde er zum Haupttäter des Genozids. Manche verehren ihn immer noch.

nzz.title: Rot-Grün lässt nicht locker: Das Zürcher Stadtparlament will Bargeldzahlungen für Sans-Papiers vor Bundesgericht erstreiten
nzz.description: Trotz geringen Erfolgsaussichten zieht der Gemeinderat ein Urteil zur wirtschaftlichen Basishilfe weiter. Der Ratspräsident gibt beim Entscheid den Ausschlag.

nzz.title: Sieben Schiessereien in fünf Tagen: In Brüssel eskaliert der Drogenkrieg
nzz.description: Der belgische Innenminister spricht von einem «nationalen Notstand». Nun haben die Behörden neue Massnahmen im Kampf gegen den Drogenhandel angekündigt. Doch längst ist das Problem ausser Kontrolle geraten.

nzz.title: Die Sturzflut trifft Pekings strategischen Korridor durch den Himalaja
nzz.description: Eine Naturkatastrophe hat einen wichtigen Grenzübergang zwischen China und Nepal zerstört. Vor einem Jahr war es schon einmal passiert. Warum halten die beiden Staaten an einer so gefährlichen Handelsroute fest?

nzz.title: War er ein Gaga-Rechtsextremist? Andreas Glarner tritt zurück
nzz.description: Der Aargauer SVP-Nationalrat und Kantonalpräsident gehört zu den umstrittensten Politikern der Schweiz. Nun gibt er seine Ämter ab. Ein Rückblick auf eine unruhige Karriere.

nzz.title: «Binnen Augenblicken war der Markt weg»: kein Entkommen bei der Flutkatastrophe in Nepal
nzz.description: Die riesige Flutwelle riss im Himalaja ganze Ortschaften fort, die Zahl der Vermissten steigt auf bis zu 1400. Auslöser könnte der Abbruch eines Gletschers gewesen sein. Die Sturzflut war so heftig, dass sie eine Erschütterung der Stärke 5,2 auslöste.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Tram fährt Fussgänger an, dieser wird weggeschleudert und von Auto erfasst – tödlich verletzt
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

observador.title: As notícias das 18h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Promessa do Governo para a Segurança Social "não vale nada"
observador.description: O líder comunista considera que o Governo "mandou o barro à parede" com o estudo da sustentabilidade do sistema de pensões e alerta para "resposta dos trabalhadores".

observador.title: Aarhus-Benfica. Marco Silva não mexe na equipa inicial
observador.description: Depois do triunfo na Luz, Benfica joga na Dinamarca com dois golos de vantagem frente ao Aarhus à procura de carimbar a entrada direta na Liga Europa. Aursnes continua de fora. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: Montenegro destaca mérito da Lei do Retorno que está no TC
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro responde a alunos da Universidade de Verão, à distância, numa sessão-surpresa comunicada apenas uma hora antes do encontro.

observador.title: A vida num minuto (e o roubo de um tesouro em quatro)
observador.description: O mundo despede-se de Dolly Parton e Yayoi Kusama. Enquanto isso, em Oslo, antecipa-se um cenário cada vez mais previsível de transição no trono norueguês, face ao agravar da saúde de Harald V.

observador.title: Afeganistão. ONG denunciam lei que proíbe manifestações
observador.description: Nova lei de 84 páginas do Ministério da Justiça afegão alarga também a detenção policial de 3 para 10 dias. Em junho, forças de segurança mataram duas pessoas numa manifestação em Herat.

observador.title: Os think tanks são a nova moda?
observador.description: O surgimento de novos movimentos de direita levanta suspeitas sobre lutas internas de poder. E ainda, o regresso dos "jobs for the boys" no emprego público e as pensões que continuam na gaveta.

observador.title: Dois mortos em ataque a escola perto de Berlim
observador.description: O alegado autor, de 19 anos, foi detido. Entre as vítimas está um homem de 30 anos que terá morrido ao tentar travar o ataque no liceu de Gosen-Neu Zittau.

observador.title: EUA. Guterres confirma pagamento de dívida "em breve"
observador.description: Perante uma grave crise de liquidez, Guterres espera um pagamento de 622,2 milhões de euros, referente às contribuições norte-americanas para o orçamento regular da ONU.

observador.title: Diretor da PJ alvo de denúncia por escuta proibida
observador.description: Diretor da PJ terá, segundo esta denúncia, mentido em tribunal sobre escuta proibida que terá ordenado. Ministra da Justiça já veio dizer que mantém confiança em Carlos Cabreiro.

observador.title: 50.ª Feira do Livro de Aveiro abre sexta-feira
observador.description: O evento, que decorre até 13 de setembro no Rossio, celebra cinco décadas com mais livreiros, sessões de autógrafos, oficinas, espetáculos e entrada gratuita.

observador.title: 17h. PS garante que não quer acelerar calendário político
observador.description: Ainda assim, o líder parlamentar dos socialistas sublinha que o partido está preparado para eleições. Ainda, a CPI sobre as polémicas em torno de Luís Neves só deve ganhar força no fim do ano.

observador.title: City, Barça, United e Liverpool no caminho dos portugueses
observador.description: FC Porto e Sporting ficaram a conhecer os adversários na primeira fase da Champions, com City a jogar no Dragão e em casa com leões. Barça, Liverpool, Nápoles, Roma e Betis também estarão nas contas.

observador.title: Drone explodiu junto à embaixada portuguesa em Kiev
observador.description: Um drone russo caiu a cerca de 300 metros da Embaixada de Portugal na Ucrânia. O ataque resultou na explosão e danos em edifícios próximos, mas sem feridos a registar.

observador.title: Ministra da Saúde admite falta de anestesiologistas
observador.description: Sindicato dos Médicos da Zona Sul alertou para "grave escassez" na ULS de São José. Ana Paula Martins confirma e promete mais vagas no internato de especialidade.

observador.title: Raimundo: viabilizar o OE é apoiar política "contra o país"
observador.description: Falando aos jornalistas depois de visita à Quinta da Atalaia, o secretário-geral do PCP avisou os dois partidos sobre a viabilização do OE, que considera ser "política contra as necessidades do país".

observador.title: Nem a surpresa escondida no meio da terra derruba o rei
observador.description: Num dia de grande trabalho da Emirates — e de Almeida —, Pogacar atacou na última subida, mas foi alcançado por Mas e quase caiu na descida. No final, bateu o espanhol ao sprint e chegou ao hat-trick.

observador.title: "Não é o PS que acelera o calendário político"
observador.description: O líder da bancada parlamentar do PS diz que há um nervosismo instalado no governo. Brilhante Dias garante ainda que não são os socialistas que aceleram o calendário político.

spiegel.title: Kanada: Könnte das Land EU-Mitglied werden?
spiegel.description: Kanada als Mitglied der Europäischen Union – das mag verrückt klingen. Aber der Zollkonflikt der USA mit dem Nachbarn belebt die Debatte über eine Idee, die man in Berlin »ungewöhnlich« findet, aber nicht undenkbar.

spiegel.title: Nepal: SPIEGEL-Reporter berichtet aus dem Katastrophengebiet
spiegel.description: Mehr als 350 Tote und 1300 Vermisste: Nach der verheerenden Sturzflut im Himalaja suchen Rettungsteams nach Überlebenden. SPIEGEL-Korrespondent Serafin Reiber ist in das Katastrophengebiet gereist. Seine Eindrücke im Video.

spiegel.title: Der Bürgermeister von Springe will den Rathausplatz nach Olivia Jones benennen. Und scheitert
spiegel.description: Olivia Jones erlebte eine schwere Jugend in der niedersächsischen Stadt Springe. Bürgermeister Springfeld würde den Travestie-Star heute gern ehren. Doch der Widerstand ist groß. Erneut.

spiegel.title: Syrien: Der Kurswechsel des Kurdenführers Mazloum Abdi
spiegel.description: Lange misstrauten die kurdisch geführten Syrischen Demokratischen Kräfte der Zentralregierung in Damaskus. Nun lösen sie sich auf – und ihr Chef soll den Mann beraten, den er einst bekämpfte. Was bedeutet das für das Land?

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Wolodymyr Selenskyj ehrt Sean Penn als »Nationale Legende«
spiegel.description: Oscarpreisträger Sean Penn gilt in Hollywood als einer der wichtigsten Unterstützer der Ukraine. Jetzt wurde er für sein Engagement von Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj ausgezeichnet – nicht zum ersten Mal.

spiegel.title: US-Armee hat offenbar »mehr als kritischen« Mangel an Raketenabwehrsystemen
spiegel.description: Dem US-Militär in Europa gehen offenbar die Raketenabwehrsysteme aus. Das meldet die Nachrichtenagentur AP und beruft sich auf Insider. Die Folgen für die Nato-Staaten könnten verheerend sein.

spiegel.title: Premier League: Leon Goretzka spielt jetzt für Aston Villa
spiegel.description: Bei den Bayern hat Nationalspieler Leon Goretzka keinen neuen Vertrag mehr bekommen. Aston Villa holt ihn nach Birmingham – und feiert den Vertrag mit einem eigenwilligen Vergleich.

spiegel.title: Cannabis-Investitionen: Profitieren CSU-Spender von neuer Cannabis-Regelung?
spiegel.description: Der Bundestag hat eine neue Regelung zu Cannabis-Medikamenten beschlossen. Der wohl größte Profiteur ist ein Münchner Hersteller. SPIEGEL-Recherchen legen nahe, dass es bei der Zulassung seines Schmerzmittels Druck von oben gab.

spiegel.title: Sankt Petersburg: Russischer Offizier stirbt bei Sprengstoffexplosion in seinem Auto
spiegel.description: In einem für Militärangehörige gebauten Viertel Sankt Petersburgs ist eine Bombe in einem Auto explodiert. Ein Offizier starb, seine Frau wurde verletzt. Es war nicht der erste Fall dieser Art.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Flutkatastrophe in Nepal, BYD und Elektro-Autos, Donald Trump und die US-Bonds
spiegel.description: Nepals Behörden rätseln über die Ursache der Flutkatastrophe, während Rettungskräfte verzweifelt nach Überlebenden suchen. Und: Chinas Elektro-Offensive trifft auf deutsche Autokrise. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz lässt die Athletinnen und Athleten im Spitzensport hängen – Meinung
spiegel.description: Der Bundeskanzler hat angekündigt, für mehr Medaillen und Sportstätten zu sorgen, auch will er Olympia nach Deutschland holen. Dabei bekommt Friedrich Merz nicht einmal den eigens dafür geschaffenen Posten nachbesetzt. Ein fatales Signal.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: 200 Tonnen Quallen legen Atomkraftwerk lahm
spiegel.description: Frankreich setzt intensiv auf Atomkraft. Nun sorgen zahlreiche Quallen erneut dafür, dass das größte Atomkraftwerk des Landes nicht wie geplant arbeiten kann. Helfen soll nun eine ungewöhnliche Maßnahme.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino: Uefa plant Strafverfahren gegen Fifa-Präsident
spiegel.description: Wegen der gescheiterten Investorenpläne für die Fußball-WM wächst der Druck auf Fifa-Chef Gianni Infantino. Die Uefa fordert nun vor einem US-Gericht Dokumente ein, Ziel ist ein Strafverfahren.

spiegel.title: DFB: Deniz Undav ringt nach WM-Aus mit Nagelsmann-Kritik
spiegel.description: Gerade ist Deutschland bei der WM gescheitert, da hebt der damalige Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann einen Fehlschuss von Deniz Undav hervor. Der Stuttgarter sagte nun, dass ihn die Szene und die Aussage bis heute beschäftigen.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Wie es zur verheerenden Sturzflut im Himalaja kommen konnte
spiegel.description: Die dramatischen Bilder vom Aufprall der Flutwelle auf einen Grenzposten zwischen China und Nepal gingen um die Welt. Wieso war die Flutwelle so gewaltig? Einschätzungen von SPIEGEL-Wissenschaftsdokumentar Marc Theodor.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Berlin: Windkraft-Betrüger Hendrik Holt nach Freigang auf der Flucht
spiegel.description: Mit Windparks, die es nicht gab, hat Hendrik Holt Energiekonzerne um Millionen Euro betrogen. Dafür sitzt er eine Freiheitsstrafe ab. Nun ist er von einem Freigang aus der JVA nicht zurückgekehrt, die Fahndung läuft.

spiegel.title: Wildlife Photography of the Year 2026: Ausgewählte Bilder des Fotowettbewerbs
spiegel.description: Fehlgeschlagene Jagdversuche, planschende Bären und eine gute Tarnung: Beim britischen »Wildlife Photographer Award« werden herausragende Tierfotos ausgezeichnet. Hier sind die besten Bilder.

phys-org.description: A new study examining death-related conceptual metaphors employed by neurosurgeon Paul Kalanithi in his memoir, "When Breath Becomes Air," sheds light on how he depicted death after being diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer at age 36.

phys-org.title: Using AI to thwart election misinformation
phys-org.description: Election rumors, such as unverified accounts of voter fraud, have run rampant in the U.S. in recent years. Powered by the speed of social media and artificial intelligence (AI), it can be hard for people to know what messages to trust. Now, a team led by Caltech researchers is using AI as a tool for good in the fight against election misinformation.

phys-org.title: Parasitic plants act like genetic engineers by stealing and remodeling useful genes
phys-org.description: Many plant species parasitize other plants by latching on and taking the nutrients their hosts need to survive. But sometimes, plants steal more than nutrients; they take genes.

phys-org.title: ATLAS and CMS narrow in on twin Higgs production
phys-org.description: Finding one Higgs boson was hard enough, but physicists at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) are hunting for something even more elusive: pairs of Higgs bosons. At the recent International Conference on High Energy Physics 2026, the ATLAS and CMS collaborations presented new constraints on the double-Higgs production rate, providing insight into how the Higgs boson interacts with itself.

phys-org.title: 'Like uprooting tree stumps'—pulling nanoscale anchors creates tiny pores that could speed biosensor manufacturing
phys-org.description: A new manufacturing method could help move the production of nanoscale sensors from specialized fabrication facilities to conventional semiconductor manufacturing plants.Publishing in Science Advances, researchers from KTH Royal Institute of Technology liken their technique to uprooting a tree stump with a rope.

phys-org.title: How rising air plumes help spike moist heat
phys-org.description: As climate change has led to more frequent extreme-heat events around the world, moist heat metrics such as wet-bulb temperature, which combines temperature and humidity, have become increasingly relevant. Days with both high heat and high humidity are dangerous to human health; understanding how these extreme events will change in the future is important.

phys-org.title: Surprising ingredients suggest ancient Egyptian paint was far more complex than previously assumed
phys-org.description: Ancient Egypt has left us a wealth of artistic treasures, including wall paintings, wooden coffins and limestone reliefs. Many retain their vibrant colors despite the passage of time, a testament to the ingredients used to make the paint mixtures. A new study published in the journal Science Advances has taken a closer look at some of the organic materials used in these painted artworks, including paint binders and adhesives.

phys-org.title: Tiny transmitters could unlock monarch migration mysteries in Florida
phys-org.description: Every spring, many monarch butterflies drift back into Florida on orange-and-black wings that have captivated scientists for generations. They arrive quietly, fluttering through fields and roadsides, stopping at nectar plants to feed and lay eggs on patches of milkweed. Soon, their offspring emerge and begin dispersing across the landscape.

phys-org.title: Emperor penguin colonies reveal decades-long resilience and flexible breeding sites
phys-org.description: With their charming waddles, heat-conserving huddles and tuxedo-like plumage, emperor penguins are among the world's most recognizable animals. Recent satellite surveys estimate that hundreds of thousands of the flightless birds live in 66 colonies spread around Antarctica's inaccessible, frozen coastlines. phys-org.title: The physics of kiiking, Estonia's extreme sport of swinging
phys-org.description: When an athlete swings upside down atop a 7-meter (23-foot) pendulum, it may seem like a feat of strength, courage or technique. A new study suggests it is something more fundamental: a striking demonstration of how intelligence emerges from the interaction of brain, body and environment.

phys-org.title: Oxygen collisions reveal how quark–gluon matter approaches equilibrium
phys-org.description: High-energy nuclear collisions recreate extreme conditions similar to those in the early universe, producing quark–gluon plasma (QGP), a hot state of matter in which quarks and gluons are no longer confined inside protons and neutrons. While large systems such as lead–lead collisions can produce matter that behaves like a fluid, collective behavior has also been observed in smaller systems.

phys-org.title: Examining discretion in revenue recognition under ASC 606
phys-org.description: New research by SUNY Polytechnic Institute (SUNY Poly) assistant professor of accounting Dr. Angelica Castro examines how changes to accounting standards have affected the way companies report revenue and the discretion managers have when making financial reporting decisions.

phys-org.title: Deep underground, SuperCDMS begins hunting light dark matter with 24 cryogenic crystals
phys-org.description: In the hunt for one of nature's most elusive substances—dark matter, which makes up 85% of all matter in the universe—scientists are going to extremes. Deep underground and chilled to near absolute zero, the Super Cryogenic Dark Matter Search (SuperCDMS) SNOLAB—one of the world's most sensitive dark matter searches—has begun collecting its first scientific data.

phys-org.title: NASA Johnson pilots chase moon's shadow for eclipse science
phys-org.description: During the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse over Europe, scientists aimed to study a long-standing mystery: why the sun's outer atmosphere, the corona, is far hotter than its visible surface. Capturing the data they needed meant being in exactly the right place at the right time.

phys-org.title: First observation of optical Magnus effect could sharpen quantum computer control
phys-org.description: Table tennis professionals are true masters at redirecting fast-moving projectiles. Putting a targeted spin on a serve can make the little white ball fly straight toward the edge of the table but then, at the last moment, take a sharp curve into the left corner. The physical phenomenon behind this sporting trick is known as the Magnus effect. It acts on balls of all sizes and has helped decide more than a few soccer matches.

phys-org.title: Pilot study finds lockable pouches help reduce smartphone use in schools
phys-org.description: Smartphone use during the school day dropped significantly across eight Northern Ireland secondary schools. Teachers reported clear behavioral benefits, though pupil well-being showed little meaningful change. Implementation challenges eased as the pilot progressed.

undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.
